The acceptance doc repeats this: 'H4 is inconsistent mediation (suppression). Each indirect effect is positive while c′ and c are negative.'

findings.area: S10 Spearman permutation-floor note (batch correlations, Holm)
findings.claim: The new S10 warning says the Holm-adjusted p of a floor pair 'cannot fall below k × .001'. That is false when the family mixes the two Spearman p-methods. A pair with ≤ 500 complete cases gets the permutation p. A pair with > 500 gets the asymptotic p, which can be much smaller and then ranks first. The floor pair then gets a Holm p of (k − rank + 1) × .001, which is below k × .001. The warning contradicts the table printed beside it. The Bonferroni wording is correct.
findings.evidence: In-memory run at 074dfbc. Spearman, adjust='holm', n = 600. other_a had 150 NaN, giving 450 pairs and the permutation p. other_b was complete, giving 600 pairs and the asymptotic p. Output: other_a p_raw=0.001 p_adj=0.001 (permutation); other_b p_raw=8.17e-89 p_adj=1.63e-88 (asymptotic). Warning: '1 pair(s) (other_a) have p = .001 … With 2 tests their adjusted p cannot fall below 0.002.' The pair's own adjusted p is shown as 0.001. Mixed methods come from correlation.py:108 (n <= 500 → permutation, otherwise asymptotic). The sentence is emitted unconditionally at batch_correlation.py:259-261.
findings.red_test: rng=np.random.default_rng(11); n=600; x=rng.normal(size=n); df=pd.DataFrame({'focal_score':x,'other_a':x+rng.normal(0,1,n),'other_b':x+rng.normal(0,1,n)}); df.loc[:149,'other_a']=np.nan; fam=correlate_many(df,'focal_score',['other_a','other_b'],method='spearman',adjust='holm',resamples=200); floor=[r for r in fam.rows if 'permutation' in r.p_method and r.p_raw<=0.001+1e-12]; assert any('cannot fall below 0.002' in w for w in fam.warnings); self.assertTrue(all(r.p_adjusted>=0.002 for r in floor))  # fails today: p_adjusted == 0.001

Every path of the path models matches textbook OLS/HC3 to 1e-9: b, SE, t, p (1e-7), CI, β, R², adj. R², F, F p, df and MSE. Cronbach's α (variance and covariance forms), the Feldt CI from F quantiles, and α-if-deleted were checked on 14 scales. v1: X .913795 [.894, .931], M .801685, W .903086, Y .812416, AVOID .690897, ASSERT .732709, all 52 coping items. v2: raw and reverse-recoded. Arbitrary levels and n, k agree exactly. The pingouin quirk (listwise uses n before deletion) is confirmed, as the docs say.

Bootstrap. It is a proper case bootstrap: indices are (B, n), each row's count has mean 1 and variance ≈ 1 − 1/n, and all equations use the same rows. My own code on the same indices reproduces every draw to ≤ 5.8e-13. Type-7 limits agree to ≤ 4.3e-14, and the bootstrap SE is exactly SD(ddof = 1). Two runs are bit-identical, and the SHA-256 I recomputed equals indices_sha256. Seed 37066, B = 5000 and the valid count are reported in BootstrapInfo, the run inputs and the methods text. The percentile type is documented in the docs and in BootstrapInfo.method.

Independent RNG check (MT19937 RandomState, 20 × 5000 resamples per configuration, 6 configurations: v1 H4/H7/H8, v2 M4, M7 two centred, M14 two centred HC3). The engine's limits and SEs fall within Monte Carlo error: max |z| = 2.64 over about 150 comparisons.

Singular resamples: with a 3-case 0/1 covariate, 260 of 5000 resamples are left out. That is exactly the number in which the dummy is constant (expected (1 − 3/n)ⁿ ≈ 4.9%), and warn.boot_invalid is emitted.

The workspace path (run_method for mediation, linear_model, conditional_process 7/14) gives the same numbers as the engine and oracles: H4 seed 37066, B 5000, 5000 valid. With no model chosen it raises RoleProblems(block.choose_option).
